model.rationale: Guthrie is a well-funded incumbent in an R+20 district, while his Democratic opponent has raised almost nothing and draws no outside spending. Markets and fundamentals both point to an easy Republican hold, so the forecast stays near the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a materially closer race or unexpected outside spending against Guthrie would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Kentucky's 2nd District is a heavily Republican seat, and Brett Guthrie is seeking another term as its incumbent. He has built a large financial advantage, raising about $4.7 million and holding $1.7 million on hand, with no outside groups spending against him. His Democratic opponent, Megan Wingfield, has raised only a few thousand dollars and has essentially no cash to compete, and no outside support has materialized for her campaign.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on the district's strong Republican lean, the incumbent's financial dominance, and prediction markets that price Guthrie's chances at roughly 96 percent. The race is rated Safe R, with Guthrie expected to win by a wide margin.
